# External Failure Evidence — Mars Climate Orbiter

Status: VERIFIED EXTERNAL EVENT

NASA/JPL states that a failure to recognize and correct an error in information transfer between teams led to the spacecraft loss. One team used English units while another expected metric units. NASA engineering material identifies inadequate systems engineering, communications, and verification among contributing factors.

Sources:
- https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/mars-climate-orbiter-team-finds-likely-cause-of-loss/
- https://swehb.nasa.gov/spaces/7150/pages/16449723/SWE-017%2B-%2BProject%2Band%2BSoftware%2BTraining
- https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20010005242/downloads/20010005242.pdf

Truth boundary:
This incident was not an AI-agent incident. The interface requirement existed. It is evidence of the cost of an undetected cross-boundary semantic mismatch, not proof that COLLIDER would have prevented the mission loss.
